summary: Iteration 5 (Knowledge Layer hardening) tested end-to-end: 44/45 pytest cases pass (97.8%). All 10 hardening requirements verified: (A) envelope wrapping with defaults & schema-driven sensitivity (public/personal/sensitive/highly_sensitive), (B) rich AI-extraction envelopes with confidence clamping [0,1] and invalid-source fallback, (C) same-value re-declaration preserves extracted_at and bumps last_confirmed_at, (D) rich per-property audit entries with full {at,event,property,previous,next,actor_type,actor_id,source_type,reason} — sensitive properties (car.plate, health.medications) correctly redacted as {redacted:true,value_type:...} — no raw plate/medication values leak in history, (E) optimistic concurrency: PATCH+PUT honor expected_version, 409 body has {error:'version_conflict',expected,current}, unconditional writes never conflict, (F) security 400s for keys with $, . , __proto__, constructor, prototype, over-length keys (>64) and values (>10k), nested $/. dict operators, NaN handled without 500 (returns 422), key 'Mileage KM' normalized to mileage_km, (G) soft-delete sets status=archived+archived_at+archive_reason; default GET returns empty sentinel; ?include_archived=true reveals; POST /restore reactivates preserving properties and adds 'restored' history event; /knowledge list respects include_archived flag, (H) atomic single-property PUT/GET/DELETE — GET on nonexistent key returns 200 with {envelope:null,value:null} (not 404), invalid key ($foo/a.b/__proto__) → 400 on GET+PUT, DELETE bumps version, (I) cross-user isolation: user B gets 404 for every knowledge endpoint on user A's node (GET/PATCH/PUT/DELETE/restore/history/properties/{key}); no-bearer → 401 on every /api/knowledge/* endpoint, (J) knowledge writes do NOT create decisions or life-graph edges (before/after counts identical after ~4 writes), (K) full iteration 1-4 regression passes: /decisions/top, resolve via real GPT-5.2 (Italian), /life-graph/nodes/{id}/graph?depth=2, legacy /priorities, /memory/ask, auth 401, (L) DEMO DRIFT FIX VERIFIED: demo@ora.app top-1 is 'Esci tra 25 minuti' with reason_tags containing 'imminent' — anchor refresh + ensure_live_imminent work; two consecutive logins do NOT grow decision count (stable). Only failure: (A/test_01) numeric-schema type coercion regression — passing 'mileage_km':'48500' as a bare string stores the value as string '48500' although value_type is correctly set to 'number'. Iteration 4 explicitly coerced this to int 48500. This is a business-logic regression in the service.py rewrite; not a test issue.

minor.issue: Numeric-schema coercion regression. Schema declares car.mileage_km type='number' unit='km'. When client sends bare string '48500', envelope stores value_type='number' (correct) but value stays as the string '48500' (should be int 48500). Fix in /app/backend/knowledge/provenance.py build_envelope() or in service.py _build_envelopes(): when schema hint.type=='number' and value is a numeric string, cast via int()/float() (int if no decimal point, else float); reject non-parseable strings with NormalizationError. Symmetric handling recommended for type='boolean' (accept 'true'/'false' strings) and type='date' (validate ISO). Iteration 4 test_14 asserted `d.properties.mileage_km == 48500` which will now fail against the new envelope shape too.

action_items: Fix numeric coercion in /app/backend/knowledge/provenance.py build_envelope(): when schema_hint.type=='number' and raw value (or envelope.value) is a str, coerce via int()/float(). Also coerce inside envelope path (rich input) not just bare values.
(Optional) Also apply coercion for schema type='boolean' (accept 'true'/'false') and validate type='date' strings look like ISO YYYY-MM-DD; reject otherwise via NormalizationError.

Update iteration 4 test_knowledge_layer.py::test_14 assertion — it asserts `properties['mileage_km'] == 48500` which is now an envelope dict; either rewrite to `properties['mileage_km']['value'] == 48500` or leave as a known-stale expectation (still fails today because coercion is missing).
No action needed for demo drift — anchor refresh + ensure_live_imminent work as designed (test_35 + test_36 both green).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to ~956 lines (auth + decisions + legacy tasks + life graph + knowledge + memory in one file). Consider splitting into routers/ before iteration 6.

knowledge/service.py is ~559 lines and mixes CRUD + audit + envelope + validation. When another module (Decision Engine consumers) starts reading envelopes, worth extracting envelope-diff + history-writer into their own submodule.

provenance.build_envelope does NOT coerce value using schema_hint.type — only fills value_type. This is the root of the numeric-string regression (see minor issue). Coercion is a natural fit for build_envelope with a small guarded helper.
server.py _ensure_live_imminent runs on EVERY successful auth. Fine today (one count_documents + one insert only if missing) but worth a metric later.

MongoDB collection `node_knowledge` unique index is on (user_id, node_id) — correct. `id` unique+sparse also correct. History array grows unbounded on hot nodes; add a compaction/cap policy in a later iteration.
seed_data_creation: Two fresh users registered per run (iter5_a_<ts>@ora.app, iter5_b_<ts>@ora.app). User A also triggers Life Graph seed via POST /api/life-graph/seed + a health node auto-created if missing. Demo user demo@ora.app is exercised for drift-fix (login-only, no writes).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with `pytest -n 0` (serial). Suite is self-contained; tests share module-scope state fixture. Only 1 minor bug left: numeric coercion in build_envelope (see action_items). All 42 other iteration-5 requirements + full iteration 1-4 regression pass — including the demo-user 'imminent' drift fix that was outstanding since iteration 3.
rca_of_issue: test_01_bare_values_wrap: `PATCH /api/knowledge/nodes/{car_id}` with body `{properties:{mileage_km:'48500'}}` returns envelope `{value:'48500', value_type:'number', unit:'km', sensitivity:'public'|'personal', provenance:{...}}`. Expected value is int 48500 per spec (schema car.mileage_km type='number'). Root cause: /app/backend/knowledge/provenance.py build_envelope() uses schema_hint only to set value_type/unit/format/sensitivity — it does NOT cast raw value to the declared type. normalize.sanitize_value() also doesn't coerce (by design — it only sanitizes). Reproduction: 1 line — `curl -X PATCH .../knowledge/nodes/<car_id> -d '{"properties":{"mileage_km":"48500"}}'` then GET; you'll see value:'48500' string. Mitigation: add a small helper `_coerce_by_type(value, target_type)` invoked inside build_envelope right before storing `env['value']`. Rules: number→int if str has no dot and is signed digits, else float; boolean→lower-cased 'true'/'false' → bool; date→validate ISO but keep as str; otherwise leave as-is. Reject uncoercible with NormalizationError so the client sees 400.
